It calls a different party-listing function (BattleParty_ListActiveMembers, not Func_080b6a60), never touches BattleWorkPtr (Data_03001e74), and its djinn/element totals logic has no call, field-offset, or constant overlap with this owner. Not used as evidence. The real callee graph -- Func_080b6a60, Func_080b7dd0, Func_080b6f44, Func_080b7424 -- instead ties this owner directly to the already-drafted siblings 080b7548.c (Summon_Refresh), 080b6f44.c, 080b6a60.c, and 080b5b18.c, which supplied the actual reconstruction evidence.

domain: Positions every active battle unit at battle start / refresh: places the active party (from Func_080b6a60) using a fixed per-slot (dx,dy) step table, then places any already-summoned creatures (from the Data_03001e74 placement's summon_slots) using dynamically computed positions from Func_080b7424, calling the shared per-unit actor setup Func_080b6f44 for both.
expressed: calls Func_080b6a60 to fill a 14-entry id buffer with up to the active party's owner ids and get the count

fills BattleWorkPtr[0x2dc..0x2e9] (14 bytes) with 0xff, then overwrites the last 6 of those bytes (0x2e4..0x2e9) with descending seed values 13..8 -- a per-id turn/render-order lookup array, reset before use

for each active party id (0-based loop index i): writes BattleWorkPtr[0x2dc+id] = i, then calls Func_080b6f44(Func_080b7dd0(id), id, dx, dy) with (dx,dy) read as a signed-byte pair from the fixed step table Data_080c2a62 at index i (the same table and (index*2, index*2+1) access idiom already proven standalone by games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/runtime/runtime_owner_55.c's Func_080b7410, though this owner reads the table inline rather than calling that leaf)

rebuilds the id buffer from Data_03001e74's placement->summon_slots (offset 0x64 within the placement, i.e. BattleWorkPtr+2+0x64), scanning while (s16) value != 0xff for up to 6 slots -- the identical count-building idiom already drafted in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080b7548.c (Summon_Refresh)
calls Func_080b7424 (LayoutSummonPositions) with the rebuilt ids/count to compute 6-entry x/z position arrays

for each rebuilt summon slot, if its id != 0xfe, calls Func_080b6f44(Func_080b7dd0(id), id, x, z) with the computed position pair -- the same source shape as 080b7548.c's final loop, but delegating to the shared Func_080b6f44 actor-setup routine instead of writing object->x/object->z directly
bounded_checks: an m2c workbench pass (tools/compiler/target/release/compiler workbench, out/workbench/080b75dc) against the actual retained assembly and agscc type context independently confirmed every loop's trip count, the 0x2dc/0x2e9 field offsets, the inline Data_080c2a62 table reads, and the placement/summon_slots offsets -- used as a cross-check on the hand trace, not as source

declaring the byte-fill loop's countdown values as plain `s32` (13 and 5, matching the reference's post-decrement-then-store-then-pointer-decrement do-while shape) instead of a for-loop or a `u8` decrementing value took the candidate from 336 candidate bytes / 186 wrong instructions down to 308 / 154: the `u8 val` version forced the compiler to emit a spurious 8-bit truncate-and-restore (adds/lsls/lsrs) around every decrement that the reference never has, and the wrong trip-count shape (n=14/n=6 with a leading `--n` in the condition) produced a different loop-count derivation than the reference's n=13/n=5 do-while

declaring the per-unit table lookup as a separately tracked `pos` counter (incremented by 2 each iteration) rather than recomputing `Data_080c2a62[i*2]` from the loop index each pass avoids a spurious extra stack spill this compiler introduces when asked to strength-reduce the multiply itself; the explicit-counter form is closer to the reference's own `lsls r6,r2,#1` + per-iteration `adds r6,#2` shape, though it does not reach the same register

caching `battle+2` into its own named `placement` pointer (matching how the reference appears to free sl/battle for a later unrelated reuse via fp) was tried and reproducibly regressed the candidate by 12-16 bytes (extra stack spill) versus repeating `FIELD(battle, type, 2+offset)` at each of the three placement access sites; kept the repeated form

the remaining residual is dominated by which physical callee-saved register (sl/r9/r8/fp) holds which long-lived value (battle pointer, order index i, id-buffer pointer, table-offset-vs-placement-pointer) at a handful of decision points -- every source respelling tried shifts which value lands in a register versus which gets a fresh literal/reload without closing the gap, consistent with this compiler's own internal register-preference order rather than a remaining control-flow or constant error

sr_route_evidence.note: asm/080b75dc.s lines 27-38 (.L0/.L1): retained do-while byte-fill loops (movs r7,#13 / subs r7,#1 / strb r2,[r3,#0] / subs r3,#1 / cmp r7,#0 / bge.n) decrement both the trip counter and the destination pointer in place rather than indexing from a fixed base -- the same shared idiom also present in 080b5f0c.s:27-32 and 080b5b18.s:33-39. This is a genuine retained-addressing signal (class b territory) but was assessed by static asm inspection only; no --flags -fno-strength-reduce vs default dual-compile was run to confirm the candidate reproduces this exact pointer-decrement shape only under -fno-strength-reduce. Not class (a): loops contain a store, not register-only spinning. Downgrade from PROOF pending the dual-compile diff.
sr_route_evidence.dual_compile: measured 2026-08-29: the pointer-decrement fill loop compiles byte-identically with and without -fno-strength-reduce (verified on 080b75dc; the idiom is not SR-gated), so the sweep improvement is a register-pressure side effect, not route evidence.
